articleTitle: Leveraging AI for Sustainable Deepfake Human Face Detection Using Transfer Learning Technique
abstract: News and live streams on social media can have a significant impact on our daily lives. In a matter of seconds, news can reach audiences worldwide, influencing the economy, politics, or individuals either positively or negatively. Nowadays, deepfake has become a hot research topic due to significant advancements in artificial intelligence, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI). People are increasingly unable to recognize between genuine and fake images, voices, and videos. The material generated by generative AI is highly realistic and completely unique. Therefore, using AI technology to detect fake content is crucial. This study applied transfer learning to four models: VGG16, VGG19, MobileNetV2, and ResNet50V2. This article proposed a new model based on VGG16, where we concatenated the input from the pre-trained VGG16 model with the output from two additional convolutional and MaxPooling layers for further feature extraction, followed by three dense layers for deeper learning. The experimental values stated that the proposed model attains significant performance over other approaches with an accuracy rate of 98.4%. The findings also show that deepfake detection may be performed well in the future by leveraging cutting-edge machine learning techniques. This should lead to more advancements in the accuracy and robustness of deepfake technology detection and, therefore, a safer and more sustainable digital future.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning-Driven Vulnerability Management: A Scalable Approach to Securing Dynamic Cloud Environments
abstract: With the evolution of cloud computing and more businesses moving their computing needs from on-premises datacenters to the cloud, security challenges have become a critical concern, especially with the rise of sophisticated cyber threats and the incorporation of artificial intelligence in attacks. This study presents an advanced framework for improving cloud security by addressing vulnerabilities through automated threat detection, machine learning-based vulnerability assessment, and rapid response mechanisms. The proposed approach differentiates itself from traditional vulnerability management by incorporating continuous monitoring, anomaly detection, and automated patch management. Public data sources, such as the National Vulnerability Database (NVD), and proprietary logs from a cloud service provider (CSP) are used to implement and evaluate this framework. Machine learning algorithms and auto-patching systems are employed to process large volumes of security data, resulting in faster identification and remediation of vulnerabilities than conventional methods. By integrating both known vulnerabilities from the NVD and real-time anomalies, the framework significantly reduces exposure time and enhances overall security posture. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the framework’s improved accuracy and efficiency in mitigating threats. This study also highlights the limitations of existing frameworks, emphasizing the need for a more proactive, high-level approach to managing vulnerabilities in dynamic cloud environments.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Explainable Artificial Intelligence Methods in Epilepsy Detection
abstract: Epilepsy is a chronic, noncommunicable disease that may cause life-threatening seizures. During a seizure attack abnormal electrical activity results in brain dysfunction. An Electroencephalogram (EEG) can be used to record these abnormalities and monitor seizure patterns. Many Machine Learning (ML) models are proposed to identify epileptic seizure patterns which generated promising results. Interpretable ML models help understand the decisions generated by the model. Therefore, we identified epileptic seizure signals using an interpretable VGG16 model. EEG signals are split into small parts and images are obtained from these small parts. These images are fed to the VGG16 model for classification. Moreover, we analyzed and compared the results generated by three Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods: SHAP, Guided backpropagation, and LIME. These methods identified and marked positively contributing features in the image to the classification. This study can help model developers select a better XAI method for epilepsy detection. The VGG16 model achieved seizure and non-seizure classification accuracy of 98.98% on the Bonn University dataset. XAI method SHAP produced the best explainability among all the three methods. Such explainability can help neurologists understand why the model has arrived at a particular decision and identified a person as an epileptic patient.

articleTitle: Glaucoma Diagnosis with Fundus Image Analysis Using Cup-To-Disc Ratios
abstract: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness globally, manifests as a gradual, stealthy progression of ocular structural changes that pose challenges for early detection. Attentive monitoring and proactive measures are essential to mitigate vision loss linked to this condition. The Cup-To-Disc Ratio (CDR) plays a pivotal role in identifying and assessing glaucoma. By comparing the dimensions of the optic cup with those of the optic disc, the CDR provides vital insights into disease progression and severity. Our study employed image processing techniques to calculate the CDR and explored its correlation with glaucomatous and healthy fundus images. Our analysis revealed significant variations in CDR values between images indicating glaucoma and those depicting normal ocular states. Particularly noteworthy is our successful differentiation of these two categories using a threshold value of 0.5. The model achieved an accuracy of 73.33%, with sensitivity and specificity values of 67% and 80%, respectively, highlighting CDR’s diagnostic utility in assessing glaucoma.

articleTitle: Enhancing Timeliness and Accuracy in Blood Transportation through Drone Technology in Saudi Arabia’s Government Clinic
abstract: Timely blood sample transportation is crucial for healthcare, particularly in emergencies, in Saudi Arabia’s government clinics, the current process involves daily noon collections by SPL logistics representatives, causing delays in testing and limited availability for urgent cases. Through consultations with a healthcare professional, we identified Key inefficiencies include restricted collection times, absence of onsite laboratories, and lengthy transportation, often exceeding an hour. This study applied business process re-engineering (BPR) to address these issues by integrating drone technology, using the Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) framework, the current process (AS-IS) was analyzed, and a future model (TO-BE) incorporating drones was developed, simulations using Bizagi revealed a significant reduction in average process time from 3 hours and 20 minutes to 1 hour and 19 minutes, the findings highlight the potential of drones to revolutionize healthcare logistics, reducing delays and improving patient outcomes, future research proposes a hybrid approach, integrating drones with traditional logistics systems for enhanced efficiency and scalability.

articleTitle: Strategies for Effective EEG Preprocessing
abstract: The administration of anesthesia is critical for ensuring the safety of surgical procedures, yet it comes with inherent risks associated with medication mistakes. Monitoring EEG signals during anesthesia is crucial for understanding patient physiology; however, the accuracy of this information heavily relies on effectively eliminating noise. Decreasing noise in EEG signals is vital for accurately interpreting data, ultimately enhancing patient safety and refining anesthesia management. This research concentrates on an advanced preprocessing technique for EEG signals, employing segmentation, detrending, variational mode decomposition (VMD), and noise reduction through Gaussian filtering, moving averages, Independent Component Analysis (ICA), and Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). The study utilized EEG data collected during surgeries and applied these preprocessing approaches to reduce noise and artifacts. Our results indicate that employing the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) for denoising is robust and produces superior outcomes compared to other techniques investigated, achieving a high Signal-To-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 43.23 dB.

articleTitle: Evaluating Compliance Costs and Their Impact on User Satisfaction and Behavior: Insights from the e-Claim System at UPSI
abstract: This study investigates the impact of compliance costs on user satisfaction and usage behavior of the e-Claim system at Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI). Data were collected from 285 administrative staff members using a structured questionnaire. The analysis reveals a significant positive correlation between usage behavior and user satisfaction, while compliance costs mediate this relationship. The findings highlight the importance of reducing compliance costs to enhance the efficiency of the e-Claim system. Practical recommendations for improving system adoption and satisfaction are discussed.

articleTitle: Profit Sharing Game for Metaverse Applications
abstract: Many foresee the Metaverse as the next evolutionary step of the internet, a perspective underscored by the volume of research surrounding it. Within the scope of this research, numerous Metaverse applications, especially those incorporating blockchain technology and immersive 3D worlds, necessitate considerable processing power and resources. Some Metaverse enthusiasts are inclined to offer their computing resources in exchange for rewards. This paper unveils a profit-sharing model anticipated to be foundational in numerous Metaverse platforms. Within this model, a plethora of processing tasks exist, each with its designated reward. Users eager to contribute their resources can select a task, aiming for the highest possible reward. However, if a task attracts multiple users, the resulting reward undergoes an equitable split. The overarching objective is the amplification of cumulative user rewards. Our findings indicate that even when users act primarily out of self-interest, the outcome achieved is no less than half of the ideal communal benefit. Further, prove that the optimal allocation of users is always Nash equilibrium and we propose an algorithm to find the optimal allocation.

articleTitle: Predictive Control MPC for wind turbine systems based DFIG
abstract: In this paper, we present a new contribution for the control of wind systems based on DFIG. The MPC predictive control offers better performance in terms of tracking and robustness compared to other controls. By using the relationship between rotor voltages and active and reactive power derivatives, the suggested algorithm, the model predictive control optimized by the FCS-MPPC finite control set, directly controls the DFIG powers. The proposed model is validated by the Matlab & Simulink environment thus the results obtained show better performance in terms of stability and efficiency, the results have been well interpreted and compared.

articleTitle: Enhancing 6G-Satellite Network Integration with Artificial Intelligence: A Future Communication Paradigm
abstract: The integration of 6G networks and satellite communications is set to revolutionize global connectivity, offering seamless coverage across terrestrial and non-terrestrial environments. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is essential for improving this integration, addressing challenges such as dynamic resource management, latency reduction, and network optimization. AI techniques like machine learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning offer innovative solutions to handle the complexities of 6G-satellite networks. These advancements promise to significantly improve network efficiency, enhance data transmission reliability, and ensure seamless connectivity across different areas. Potential use cases include smart cities, autonomous vehicles, and Internet of Things (IoT) applications, where AI-driven 6G-satellite integration will be crucial. The proposed AI-enhanced 6G-satellite framework not only addresses current challenges but also lays the groundwork for a resilient, scalable, and globally interconnected communication infrastructure, offering a promising future.

articleTitle: VHF Band III Spectrum Availability and Utilization for Cognitive Radio Implementation in Malaysia
abstract: The VHF Band III spectrum (174-230 MHz), recognized for its low utilization, was opened by the FCC in 2002 for opportunistic use by communication technologies. This paper presents a quantitative analysis of the availability of VHF Band III for cognitive radio CR access in Malaysia. Measurements were conducted over a week in 18 Malaysian cities to analyze spectrum utilization and received signal strength, alongside the impact of broadcasts from neighboring countries. The findings highlight actual utilization patterns and reveal the spectrum’s potential for opportunistic access, especially post-digital switchover (DSO).

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for Deepfake Image Detection Using Deep Learning Approach
abstract: Deepfake, fast growing field in the age of multimedia and AI, have been attracted attention in the recent years. Deep learning algorithms are used to create real digital content which are difficult to distinguish from authentic content. Deepfakes can serve multiples purposes, including educational content, academic research, social entertainment so it spread wrong information, information manipulation, damage to reputation, many frauds. Day to day deepfake crime is increasing. Detection of deepfake is big challenging issue in the digital forensics. A strong approach needs to be created from protecting against the media deepfake. The main work of this paper is to build a efficient framework for deepfake detection. The paper discusses deepfakes, detection techniques, datasets, proposed model. Novel proposed approach has been created that are based on the integration of CNN and VGG16. The deepfake dataset has been used to utilized the network architecture. Proposed model has been achieved the 95% accuracy and 94% precision score. The developed model is superior than the other state of art developed methods.

articleTitle: Automated Integration of BIM and 3D GIS for Sustainable Infrastructure Management
abstract: In this paper, we present an automated integration approach for BIM and 3D GIS data about infrastructure projects to improve human-machine interaction with respect to sustainable project management. Based on the step-by-step process that starts with the preparation of data in BIM about buildings and complex infrastructures, CAD for the buried networks and terrain models, and BIM itself for buildings and complex infrastructures by generating IFC models. This is followed by a cleansing and optimisation step to find geometric conflicts. ETL processes automate the development of a unified spatial database integrating BIM and GIS data, without loss to geometric or attribute data. Automation tools are used to transfer data between BIM and GIS environments. This process enables the design of a 3D GIS application for 3D visualization and advanced spatial queries, such as efficient monitoring and decision making. From a case study in preliminary infrastructure projects, such as underground networks and building structure mapping, significant improvements in workflow efficiency were observed, improving by 30%, and data errors were reduced by 20% compared to manual methods. It is an essential gain for infrastructure integration and management, in particular within the complex environments involving smart cities. This approach contributes to sustainable infrastructure management through the use of global real-time views about projects.

articleTitle: Word Recognition: A Comparative Study of Physical and Digital Media and Their Influence on improving QURAN Reading
abstract: This paper deals with a test conducted on 110 people to measure the ability to recognize the words of the Qur’an through 3 different media: 1-the traditional Qur’an page, 2-the interactive phone application (Alwah), in which the words are separated, and 3-(Alwah) printed model printed. The study aims to show which of these methods has the ability to improve the reading skills through recognizing and remembering the form of a word. Through memorization and repetition, then testing the words he recognized. Participants were asked to recognize 12 words (represented by the first verse of Surat Al-Bayyinah) after being repeatedly taught 3 times, then 6 times, then 9 times, and finally 12 times. The number and percentage of words recognized were recorded for each participant. The results showed that (Alwah) printed model was superior to the other two methods in achieving a recognition rate for more words and a lower number of repetitions. In addition, there was no significant difference between the groups.

articleTitle: Real-Time Hardware Demonstration of Innovative Technology for Cleaning of Solar PV Modules
abstract: The climate change, depletion of resources, sustainability and energy security are the major concerns globally, therefore becomes important to harness technology for sustainable solutions. The energy transition is the shift from dependence on fossil fuels to renewable and sustainable energy resources. This change addresses the urgent need for sustainable, environment friendly energy solutions which is one of the key targets of the vision 2030 of KSA. The power generation from renewable energy resources particularly solar photovoltaic may fulfill the power requirements due to its abundant availability. However, Solar PV power generation faces certain limitations, With dust buildup on solar PV modules being a significant challenge, especially in desert regions such as Saudi Arabia. This research focuses on investigating The effect of dust on the efficiency of solar PV modules, and provide an innovative technology to mitigate the impact of dust accumulated on PV modules. A laboratory prototype is developed to demonstrate the technology. The PV module is cleaned using pressurized clean water, which is sprayed through flat type nozzles to wash the upper surface of the PV modules. Wastewater from the PV module's top is collected, purified, and piped to the water storage tank. Cleaning system water recovery is 95% and water demand is 2.5 Litre/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of PV module area. Analyzing the power of clean and dusty PV modules reveals that the presence of dust has an impact on the power production from PV modules. The cleaning process boosts the PV modules' efficiency to 99% of their original value in just 2.47 minutes of operation. Based on the obtained results it is concluded that the developed technology is cost effective and may be utilized at large scale.

articleTitle: Engineering Quantum Dots: Overcoming Challenges in Telecommunications and Human-Machine Interaction
abstract: Engineering the inhomogeneity, density, composition, and aspect ratio of self-assembled quantum dots (SAQDs) is essential for various applications, from broadband technologies to telecommunications. This paper investigates the optimization of molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) grown quantum dots in the intrinsic region of optoelectronic devices, such as lasers, highlighting the need for tailored approaches based on specific applications. For instance, superluminescent diodes used for imaging require highly inhomogeneous dots, while inhomogeneity can pose challenges for SAQD lasers in telecommunications, as non-homogeneous QDs may become parasitic and hinder lasing efficiency. This study explores quantum dot lasers by adjusting the thickness of the GaAs spacer layers, which are grown at low temperatures and situated between the dot layers. Our findings reveal enhanced performance in SAQD laser structures, achieving "no blue shift" in peak emission wavelengths—critical for human-machine interaction and photonic integrated circuit applications. Maintaining stable emission wavelengths significantly boosts the efficiency of communication systems and quantum computing platforms, facilitating rapid data processing and interaction between machines and users.

articleTitle: Digitization of Medical Data: LLM-Based Data Entry, Cleansing, and Visualization Solutions
abstract: Healthcare data management faces several challenges, including errors from manual data entry, variations in data quality, and an increasing need for advanced tools to efficiently handle large datasets. This paper introduces Data-Care, an innovative application designed to automate medical record digitization by leveraging advanced technologies such as Large Language Models (LLMs), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and NoSQL databases. Together, these technologies significantly reduce the need for manual input, minimizing errors and enhancing data accuracy. A key feature of Data-Care is its data cleansing module, which resolves issues like data inconsistencies and missing values, ensuring the integrity and accuracy of the dataset. Additionally, the application provides a powerful offline visualization tool, enabling healthcare professionals to generate comprehensive reports that support informed decision-making and streamline workflows across various healthcare processes. Extensive performance tests demonstrated that the integration of LLMs and OCR in Data-Care achieved accuracy rates between 76% and 93%, depending on the quality of the input data. These results underscore Data-Care's capacity to improve both the speed and accuracy of data entry, offering a robust solution for the digitization and management of healthcare data.

articleTitle: Redefining Protein Structure Prediction: Insights from AlphaFold’s Methodology and Applications
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of AlphaFold, a pioneering algorithm developed by DeepMind, which has revolutionized the field of protein structure prediction. Since its introduction at CASP13, AlphaFold has achieved remarkable success in predicting protein structures from amino acid sequences with unprecedented accuracy. AlphaFold2 further improved upon its predecessor, integrating deeper biological insights and achieving near-experimental precision in structure predictions. In this study, we explore the methodologies that underpin AlphaFold’s success and investigate its practical applications in drug discovery, disease modeling, and broader scientific research. By replicating key components of AlphaFold’s workflow and excluding homologous structure templates, this research provides hands-on insights into its mechanisms and the challenges of static structure predictions. Furthermore, we propose strategies to address these limitations, focusing on the integration of dynamic protein simulations and advanced machine-learning models. Our findings underscore the transformative role of artificial intelligence in computational biology, with significant implications for the future of protein science and biomedical innovation.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Digital Media Content using a Smart Drone and an Innovative ML Technique
abstract: In the contemporary digital age, the fields of journalism and social media assume a pivotal role in disseminating information about current events and issues to the public. However, conventional techniques for gathering news and capturing images frequently encounter constraints and limitations. In recent years, technological advancements have transformed the creation and consumption of digital media content. This study presents an innovative solution that combines a smart drone with a reinforcement learning (RL) machine learning technique to enhance digital media content in a timely manner. The proposed framework has been subjected to validation and testing in a real-world scenario in Taif City through the transfer of rich digital media content. The results demonstrate promising outcomes, which support Saudi Arabia's efforts to enrich digital media content for tourism.

articleTitle: Travel Persona-Based Destination Recommendations for Enhancing Tourism in Saudi Arabia
abstract: In recent years, the tourism in Saudi Arabia has experienced rapid growth, accompanied by a rising demand for personalized travel experiences. With the integration of AI, this vision can become a reality by developing traveler personas that recommend destinations based on individual preferences. Our approach involves creating a high-quality dataset sourced from various platforms and preprocessing it to ensure accuracy and consistency. The recommendation system uses this data to deliver improved persona-based suggestions that enhance tourist satisfaction. The primary goal of this project is to increase visitor satisfaction and support Vision 2030’s objective of positioning Saudi Arabia as a leading global tourism destination.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning for Wind Speed Forecasting in the Desert
abstract: Wind energy and renewables, in general, would lead the way for changing the worldwide electricity industry and assist countries to meet Paris climate aims of reducing CO2 emissions by 2050. However, wind energy production is unstable due to weather changes. Managing smart energy systems mandates accurate power output prediction. Novel wind energy forecasting methods based on deep learning (DL) have achieved competitive performance compared to traditional methods. Nevertheless, they need big data for training and testing. This paper studies the feasibility of using transfer learning (TL) to develop DL models for hour-ahead wind speed (WS) prediction in a hot desert climate. It also presents the forecasting results of a DL model for data gathered from four locations in Saudi Arabia with different terrains to identify the success factors of using TL for WS prediction in a desert climate.

articleTitle: Predicting Used Cars Prices in the Egyptian Market: A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Valuing used cars in the Egyptian market poses a significant challenge due to the scarcity of new vehicles and high inflation. Consequently, used cars dominated the Automotive market, causing price fluctuations and creating a complex pricing environment. Automating the valuation process presents a valuable opportunity to save time and minimize pricing errors. This study explores the use of machine learning models to predict used car prices using data scrapped from popular online listings websites. It compares the performance of top-performing algorithms, according to previous research, including XGBoost, Random Forest Regression, and Bagging Regressor when trained on price-range segmented data versus the full dataset to determine the optimal model. Results indicated that applying price-range segmentation reduced the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 23% compared to training without segmentation. XGBoost outperformed other models, achieving an MAE of 47,478, compared to 48,829 for both Random Forest Regression and Bagging Regressor.

articleTitle: A Scalable, Portable, and Decentralized Power Solution Using Thin-Film Solar Panels with Integrated Energy Storage
abstract: Reliable access to affordable energy is essential for social and economic development, particularly in underprivileged and off-grid regions. This paper presents a portable photovoltaic (PV) system that utilizes innovative thin-film solar panels to improve energy access for decentralized communities without requiring a bulky mounting structure. The proposed system comprises a PV panel, a battery, and power conditioning circuitry, all within a compact form, capable of supplying DC power within this framework, but with the potential of conditioning for AC power if needed. Key features emphasize ease of installation, cost efficiency through minimized structural requirements and scalability to accommodate varying energy demands. This paper details the system’s operation, specifications, and testing results, highlighting its potential as a sustainable energy solution.

articleTitle: Classifying Speech Disorders Using Voice Signals and Machine Learning
abstract: This study explores the application of machine learning (ML) and advanced voice signal analysis to classify speech disorders, including vocal tremors, dysarthria, and stuttering. These disorders pose significant challenges to communication and quality of life, requiring precise and reliable diagnostic tools. To address the inherent challenges of limited data availability in this domain, the study employs synthetic voice data generated using mathematical models to augment real-world recordings. This hybrid approach ensures a more comprehensive dataset, enabling robust training and evaluation of machine learning models.Key machine learning algorithms such as Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting are utilized to extract and analyze a wide range of acoustic features from speech samples. These methods are selected for their ability to handle complex, nonlinear patterns and to identify subtle distinctions between normal and disordered speech. By leveraging these techniques, the study investigates their performance in accurately classifying speech disorders, emphasizing their potential in improving diagnostic outcomes.The findings highlight the transformative potential of machine learning in the field of speech pathology. ML models demonstrated notable improvements in the precision, efficiency, and consistency of diagnosing speech disorders compared to traditional methods. This breakthrough not only enhances diagnostic reliability but also equips clinicians with objective tools that reduce subjectivity in assessments. Moreover, the integration of these technologies promotes earlier detection of disorders, enabling timely and tailored therapeutic interventions.By facilitating more accurate and accessible diagnostic practices, this work paves the way for significant advancements in patient care. The use of ML-powered tools can bridge the gap between clinical expertise and technological innovation, empowering healthcare professionals to offer personalized treatment plans. Ultimately, this approach has the potential to improve patient outcomes, reduce the stigma associated with speech disorders, and ensure more equitable access to high-quality care for individuals worldwide.

articleTitle: Development of an Intelligent GUI with ChatGPT for Efficient and Accurate Transformer Fault Diagnosis Using DGA, Duval Triangle Method, and Machine Learning Automation
abstract: This study presents an intelligent graphical user interface (GUI) for transformer fault diagnosis, utilizing Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA), the Duval Triangle method, and automated machine learning model selection. Key gases—Methane (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>), Ethylene (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>), and Acetylene (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)—are analyzed to classify fault types, including partial discharges and thermal/electrical faults, through gas concentration ratios. The system leverages TPOT's model selection capabilities, with the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) emerging as the optimal classifier, achieving over 95% accuracy. The GUI, developed using Gradio, enables CSV uploads for batch processing and real-time fault classification, complemented by ChatGPT-generated explanations and maintenance suggestions. A case study on mineral oil-based transformers demonstrates the tool's high diagnostic accuracy, user-friendly design, and potential for expanded applications in predictive maintenance.

articleTitle: Measuring the Performance of AI-Generated Animations: Strengths, Weaknesses, and Future Directions
abstract: Generative AI has rapidly advanced in producing visually appealing animations, but its ability to capture the subtle complexities of traditional animation techniques remains insufficiently explored. This study provides a detailed evaluation of AI-generated animations through the lens of the 12 classical principles of animation, which are essential for creating lifelike and engaging motion. Utilizing expert evaluations combined with robust statistical methods, including Chi-square tests and logistic regression, we quantitatively compare AI-generated animations to traditional hand-crafted ones. Our findings reveal that while AI-generated animations perform well in static principles such as Staging, Solid Drawing, and Appeal, they consistently fail to replicate dynamic principles like Squash and Stretch, Follow-Through, and Anticipation. This analysis represents the first quantitative benchmark of AI's performance in animation, offering critical insights into its strengths and shortcomings. We conclude with specific recommendations for improving generative AI models, particularly in motion dynamics, and outline future research directions to bridge the gap between AI-driven and traditional animation techniques.

articleTitle: Automating Neural Model Selection in Spiking Neural Networks Using AutoML Techniques*
abstract: The selection of optimal neural models in Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) traditionally depends on a trial-and-error approach, which is both time-consuming and sometimes tends to suboptimal selection of the neural model. This research study explores the integration of Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) techniques into SNNs to simplify the process of designing an SNN model by automatically selecting the most optimal neural model. For example, in traditional neural networks, AutoML proves that it has the potential to significantly reduce the time and effort required to identify the best-performing architectures, by automating the selection and updating of loss functions and hyper-parametric values. To this end, we present a stand-alone framework for applying AutoML in SNNs, highlighting how this approach can improve accuracy, efficiency, and reliability in the selection process of optimal neural models, as these neural models are the core principle of designing SNN architecture. The proposed method not only accelerates the development of SNN models but also enhances their performance by systematically identifying optimal configurations that might be overlooked through manual methods. Therefore, to validate our approach, the proposed architecture was tested using different well-known benchmarks with different sets of neurons, ranging from 100 to 3000 neurons, and demonstrated state-of-the-art results in image classification tasks.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Optimization based Control for Heat Integrated Distillation Column
abstract: Controlling nonlinear heat integrated distillation column (HIDiC) systems is notably challenging due to their complex dynamics and inherent nonlinearities. This study examines the effectiveness of genetic algorithm (GA) optimization in enhancing proportional-integral (PI) controller performance for HIDiC systems. A nonlinear mechanistic model of a HIDiC was adopted, with the GA applied to tune the PI controllers for optimal control performance. Control performance was tested under varying setpoints and feed composition disturbances. Simulation results demonstrate that the GA-tuned PI controller provides robust control performance, maintaining stability and high product purity even with significant disturbances. Initial oscillations due to feed composition disturbance are minimal and quickly settle down, confirming the controller's capability to achieve precise control and high separation performance.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Grid-Connected PV System Faults Using MATLAB/Simulink
abstract: Grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems are crucial to modern renewable energy strategies, but various types of faults can significantly impact their performance. Understanding the behavior of these faults is essential for improving system reliability and reducing maintenance costs. This paper investigates the impact of common faults, including open-circuit, short-circuit, partial shading, and grid faults, by simulating them using MATLAB/Simulink. The focus is on modeling faults that lead to power output reduction. The simulation results demonstrate how different fault types affect critical system parameters, such as grid voltage and active power output. The study highlights the value of simulation as a flexible approach for exploring fault scenarios, providing insights into fault detection and mitigation strategies that can help optimize PV system performance and support the development of robust fault data collection, detection, and classification techniques.

articleTitle: Contemplating and Visualizing Gameful Experience (GAMEX) in Education Through Bibliometric Analysis of Literature
abstract: Gameful experience (GAMEX) refers to integrating game-like elements and mechanics into educational contexts to enhance engagement, motivation, and learning outcomes. The purpose of utilizing bibliometric literature analysis is to explore the publication trends and thematic clusters and identify critical areas of focus, influential researchers and publications, and gaps in the current state of GAMEX research. We developed a research question to understand the trends related to GAMEX in education thoroughly. To achieve the aims of this study, we collected data from the Scopus database. The dataset in the study comprises 90 documents with a timespan of 2005 to 2024. Further, R-studio software is used to tabulate and visualize the analyzed data. The key findings indicate prominent research growth trends, with countries like Spain and Finland leading contributors to the quantity and impact of research publications in this field. The benefits of GAMEX in education are well-supported due to its ability to foster soft skills. For upskilling, educational institutions train faculty members to integrate online activities within the course content for students' digital skills development.

articleTitle: The Relationship Between Social Media Usage and Aggressive Behavior Among Secondary School Students in Muallim District
abstract: This study explores the relationship between social media usage and aggressive behavior among secondary school students in the Muallim district, Malaysia. Using a quantitative approach, data were collected from 335 students through self-reported surveys. Social media engagement was measured by daily screen time, while aggression levels were assessed using the Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire. Statistical analysis, including Pearson correlation, revealed a significant positive relationship between prolonged social media usage and higher aggression scores (r = 0.162, p = 0.003). The findings suggest that interventions such as screen time monitoring, content moderation, and digital literacy programs tailored to age groups are necessary to mitigate the negative behavioral impacts of social media. This study provides critical insights for educators, parents, and policymakers in developing strategies to promote healthier online behaviors among Malaysian adolescents.

articleTitle: Cognitive Radio Receiver Design Employing Pipeline Successive Approximation ADC
abstract: Smart cities require better cellular communication, incorporating a high data rate that satisfies the Internet, cloud computing, and the Internet of Things (IoT) requirements. A high data rate demands higher bandwidth with low latency. However, the already saturated or underutilized frequency spectrum hinders this realization. 5G and cognitive radio technology can enhance spectrum utilization to meet the high data demands of future cellular communication. Cognitive radio uses spectrum sensing to identify underutilized frequencies without interfering with licensed users, addressing the scarcity of the electromagnetic spectrum. In this paper, a cognitive radio receiver design with a SAR analog-to-digital converter, which is recognized for having a modest resolution for high bandwidth signals, is implemented. Moreover, the pipeline technique in the SAR design is proposed to increase the resolution to be suitable for 5G applications. The high-level model of the system is simulated using MATLAB Simulink software. The quantization error observed in the regular SAR ADC design is compared to that in the proposed pipeline SAR ADC, highlighting the enhanced accuracy and efficiency of the pipeline SAR ADC, which makes it suitable for spectrum sensing in next-generation cognitive radio systems.

articleTitle: Blind Spots Detection in Autonomous Robots using Data Fusion and Deep Learning
abstract: The adoption of humanoid robots has surged in recent years, particularly in addressing operational limitations. This study introduces a methodology for detecting blind spots and anomalies in robot motion, using the Nao Robot as a case study.The approach integrates multisensor data with deep learning techniques validated on a proprietary dataset covering diverse real-world scenarios, including dynamic non-visible obstacles. High-frequency sensor sampling (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = 0.2 s) ensures accurate data, while DBSCAN clustering and ANOVA F-value-based feature selection identify critical features like obstacle distances and motion parameters for collision prediction.Deep Learning with Sigmoid and ReLU activations, the ADAM optimizer, and Sparse Categorical Crossentropy loss achieved a 95% F1 score and 99% AUC-ROC, demonstrating robust performance in dynamic environments also in real life environment.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional DOA Zero-Forcing Precoding for Enhanced Spectral Efficiency in Cell-Free Massive MIMO
abstract: Energy and spectral efficiency in mobile networks are enhanced by Cell-free Massive-MIMO systems utilizing macro-diversity to optimize overall performance. However, multi-user interference, especially due to pilot reuse within the same cell, continues to pose significant challenges. This research introduces a Two-Dimensional Direction of Arrival (2D-DOA) Zero-Forcing Precoding method. It addresses both intra-cell and inter-cell interference, removing the requirement for Channel State Information exchange between Access Points (APs). A new expression for downlink spectral efficiency is developed, considering the impacts of imperfect CSI and pilot contamination. Utilizing UESPRIT and MUSIC -based 2D-DOA estimation techniques, the proposed method surpasses pilot-contaminated systems and deterministic Zero-Forcing precoding, demonstrating enhanced spectral efficiency even under constrained pilot resources.

articleTitle: Cross-Domain Adaptation Through Adversarial Teaching for Unmanned Ariel Vehicles in Smart Cities
abstract: Person re-identification has been an important issue of surveillance systems in smart cities. However, this requires huge datasets to supervise deep learning models for accurately identifying and tracking people in smart cities. In this paper, we propose adversarial learning in integration with a mutual mean teaching model known as adversarial teaching to take the issue of domain adaptation. Initially, they learn a source dataset in a supervised way. This model information is then transferred to another model through unsupervised learning and pseudo-labels are generated by generative adversarial learning. The multi-class invariance is handled by adversarial learning. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated on two different datasets source and target datasets. Multiple experiments on Duke and Market datasets indicate higher accuracy of F-1 score on both datasets compared to previous methods, demonstrating the superior performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Vehicular Service Allocation with MEC Dynamic Task Offloading in a Dammam District Using CloudSim-SUMO
abstract: The current paper therefore discusses the significance of effective task-offloading strategies especially in an urban environment due to the evolution of means to boost both service provision and customer satisfaction. More precisely, we look into issues and opportunities in offloading vehicular services in realistic urban conditions with more reference to cities of Saudi Arabia. The research explores the application of VEC through using MEC strategies in that helps to offload computationally intensive tasks from the vehicles to the edge servers minimising resource consumption. By considering some of the important factors such as movement of vehicles, network delay and load, we present a dynamic task-offloading model that seeks to reduce delay times and energy usage while at the same time offering high service quality. The efficiency of the model is established through CloudSim-SUMO simulations comparing actual and simulated traffic in the Dammam District. We have established constant connectedness and effective task execution even with a highly mobile vehicle environment. This work is useful in developing the smart transport systems of Saudi Arabia by adding solutions that improve vehicular services and solve issues associated with ITS.

articleTitle: Smart Synergies: Integrating Technologies for Sustainable Urban Planning and Smart City Education - A Case Study
abstract: The study focuses on the use of intelligent technologies in sustainable town planning and smart city learning, both of which are needed to solve new urban problems. According to recent studies, there is a knowledge gap about studies related to smart urban planning and smart city studies The purpose of this study is to propose a way of smart city education and sustainable urban planning with necessary modern technology prioritizing citizen engagement and environmental sustainability. The principal objective of the study is to provide research-based recommendations on incorporating field-based activities in the course of smart city education. To accomplish this objective, the study uses five in-depth case studies. Each of the three case studies are real case. The potential implication of the study is to transform urban planning education, thus enhancing the participation of citizens in urban and city development. The findings provide a holistic approach by integrating technology, urban planning, and sustainability to improve urban living for sustainable, future smart city developments. This research hopes to provide insight into how new and existing technologies can create improved and more efficient urban areas across the globe.

articleTitle: Automated Motawif Monitoring Hajjis through the Pilgrimage Period
abstract: This study explores the development and evaluation of an automated application, E-Motawif, aimed at enhancing the Hajj and Umrah pilgrimage experience. The application addresses the significant challenges of managing large crowds and ensuring the safety and well-being of millions of pilgrims annually. By integrating cutting-edge Information and Communication Technologies (ICT), the Internet of Things (IoT), and Artificial Intelligence (AI), the proposed solution emphasizes safety, efficient crowd management, and a spiritually enriching journey for pilgrims. Aligned with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 and the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals, the project bridges technological advancement with sustainable urban planning strategies. The methodology incorporates the integration of advanced algorithms, such as semantic similarity using SentenceTransformer and fuzzy matching, to optimize a lost and found system and key functionalities like real-time tracking,and health monitoring. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining these techniques, achieving a balance between accuracy and user-friendly interactions. The findings highlight the importance of intuitive user interfaces, robust security measures, and accessibility across diverse demographic groups. This work contributes to the development of a safer, more organized, and environmentally conscious pilgrimage experience, blending tradition with modern technology to meet the evolving needs of pilgrims and stakeholders.

articleTitle: Exploiting Artificial Intelligence Approaches to Augment Decision-making Processes for an Intelligent Performance in Football
abstract: The world of Football has witnessed remarkable advancements, elevating the sport from being merely "The Beautiful Game" to a realm where numbers and data hold immense significance. While some clubs and teams have achieved success through research, there is a pressing need for further investment in research, particularly with the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. AI has the potential to revolutionize team performance analysis by providing real-time insights and facilitating the analysis of instant games. An illustrative instance of the application of reinforcement learning for the purpose of analyzing player styles and conducting comparative assessments among various players can significantly enhance the simulation of these players within video games, such as FIFA games. Furthermore, it can augment the process of recruiting new players in accordance with the distinct training methodologies employed by individual clubs within diverse leagues.In this paper, we propose a novel approach to developing an intelligent system that can analyze and predict Football players' performances in real-time. Our approach utilizes machine learning and deep learning techniques, as well as a recommendation system, to comprehensively analyze players' performance. This proposed system aims to support managers and players in making informed decisions by providing them with valuable insights based on diverse data sources. By leveraging this system, teams can enhance their performance and potentially attain higher international rankings.

articleTitle: Ensuring Sustainable Safety in Fine-Grained Android Permission Model: Decidability through Finite Attribute Range Constraints
abstract: When Android was first introduced, it permitted unrestricted access to all installed applications, posing significant security risks. In one of our previous works, we proposed, implemented, and demonstrated a comprehensive model capable of restricting access to sensitive permissions based on granular constraints. This model was partially adopted by Android and is now a standard feature in all modern Android-based systems. However, the flexibility of this model introduces a critical issue: the safety of the model. A model’s safety determines whether the policies enforced by the model achieve the desired security goals. In this paper, we investigate the safety and undecidability problems associated with the model and demonstrate that, in its full form, the model is undecidable. To ensure creation and maintenance of sustainable security policies at both the individual and enterprise level, we propose the addition of a Finite Attribute Range Constraint, which renders the model both decidable and safe.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Enhancing the Effectiveness of Decision-Making from Faculty Members' Point of View in Colleges of Administrative Sciences at Saudi Universities
abstract: This study investigates, in line with Saudi Vision 2030, the transforming possibilities of artificial intelligence (AI) in improving administrative decision-making inside the Colleges of Administrative Sciences at Saudi institutions. Based on past studies and a poll of eighty-five faculty members from four different colleges, the paper shows how artificial intelligence may help to enhance planning, efficiency, and decision accuracy. The results expose notable variation in AI adoption across institutions driven by institutional opposition, insufficient resources, and technological constraints. Demographic analysis emphasizes nationality as a determinant of opinions about artificial intelligence's efficiency. The paper emphasizes the importance of policy development, infrastructure spending, faculty development, and incentives to remove obstacles for artificial intelligence integration. Among the recommendations include encouraging institutional clarity, matching artificial intelligence initiatives with national development objectives, and advancing cooperation. This study confirms that artificial intelligence has the ability to transform decision-making procedures by means of structural and cultural difficulties addressed, therefore allowing Saudi institutions to attain higher administrative effectiveness and support larger developmental goals.

articleTitle: TeacherEye: An AI-Powered System for Monitoring Student Engagement in Online Education
abstract: In online education, maintaining student engagement and academic integrity poses significant challenges. While multiple solutions have been introduced, none have provided a comprehensive system. We introduce TeacherEye, an Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered system for monitoring student behavior and engagement in virtual classrooms and exams. TeacherEye integrates State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) AI models to analyze video data from the webcam stream and audio data from the micro-phone in real time. The system first verifies students through face detection and identification. It then monitors behavior using advanced vision features like sleep detection, multi-person detection, phone usage detection, focus tracking, and emotion recognition. Audio is simultaneously converted to text and analyzed by a Large Language Model (LLM) to detect suspicious behavior, enhancing online exam proctoring. If irregularities are found, a Vision-Language Model (VLM) suggests actions to the teacher, while all detected behavior is logged for review. TeacherEye presents a comprehensive solution for improving engagement and ensuring integrity in online education.

articleTitle: Harnessing Deep Learning for Enhancing Brain Tumor Classification in a Sustainable Healthcare Environment
abstract: Brain tumor affect human health owing to their location. Early detection plays a pivotal role in improving treatment efficacy and patient outcomes. Computer-Aided detection systems, leveraging medical imaging techniques, have emerged as valuable tools for assisting clinicians in diagnosing cancer. Deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks, has shown remarkable promise in medical image analysis, offering enhanced accuracy and efficiency. This study employed transfer learning and deep neural networks for the classification of brain tumors into its different classes. The pre-trained CNN models, used in the classification were EfficientNet, ResNet, DenseNet, and Xception and a series of image pre-processing and augmentation were carried out before feeding the images to the classification models to enhance classification performance. Four ensemble models were built after getting the results from the classification models, ICAVG for image classification average predictions, ICMAX for image classification maximum predictions, FCAVG for extracted features classification average predictions, and FCMAX for extracted features classification maximum predictions. The results from these four ensemble models were again combined into CAVG for the average results of both ICAVG and FCAVG, and CMAX for the maximum results from both ICMAX and FCMAX. The proposed model was tested on a brain tumor dataset of 3064 samples and the investigational validation of the proposed technique portrayed a superior accuracy value of 99.02% over existing models. Based on high predictive results this research work endeavors to contribute to the advancement of cancer diseases detection, facilitating early diagnosis and improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning and Time-Domain Feature Mining based Appliance Power Consumption Pattern Recognition
abstract: As technology has advanced, using smart meters instead of conventional ones has changed. These smart meters are essential parts of intelligent grids, offering significant advantages to many stakeholders regarding social, environmental, and economic constraints. A detailed method of fine-grained collection and analysis of the metering data is necessary to benefit the different smart grid stakeholders. This results in collecting, transmitting, and processing a large amount of data with an exponentially raised dimension. It seriously constrains the system processing resources, latency, data management, transmission effectiveness, and analysis response time. In this regard, a new hybridization of ensemble learning and time-domain feature extraction is suggested for the automatic classification of appliances through the processing of their power consumption data. Time-domain feature mining makes up for the previously noted deficiency and can result in a considerable real-time data dimension reduction without sacrificing important information. Data in compressed form can therefore be processed, examined, stored, and transmitted with efficiency. It offers a significant reduction in the post cloud-based classification latency along with computational and transmission effectiveness. The classification is carried out using the robust ensemble learning (EL) classifiers. The performance of considered EL classifiers is evaluated for the case of a real multi-class and multi-device smart meter dataset. The devised solution achieves a highest average classification accuracy of 88.33% for a 10-class problem while securing a compression gain of 32.73.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning and Event-Based Feature Mining for Li-Ion Battery State Prediction
abstract: Contemporary power solutions are revolutionizing the existing trend in residential and transportation services. Mobile realizations, in particular, are advancing based on innovative mobile power supply solutions. Batteries are essential to several key applications, such as electric vehicles (EVs), satellites, and mobile phones. Additionally, batteries are elementary parts of the energy storage for distributed renewable microgrids. The are just a few applications based on the batteries-based power supply. Li-ion batteries are frequently used because of their exceptional qualities, which include endurance, high power density, and compact size. Besides these notable benefits the Li-Ion batteries are expensive. To effectively compensate for this high initial cost, the "battery management systems" (BMSs) are used. These solutions are effective in maximizing the Li-Ion battery life and also guarantee a safer operation. Based on the advantages of modular design, the contemporary Li-Ion batteries can be comprised of thousands of individual cells. It results in complex and sophisticated BMSs and can render a notable overhead in terms of power consumption. The focus of this research is on enhancing the existing Li-Ion BMSs by incorporating novel event-based feature mining and machine/ensemble learning techniques. The event-based feature extractor mines pertinent information and promises significant real-time compression. In order to predict the capacity of Li-Ion cells, the produced feature set is then processed utilizing robust machine/ensemble learning algorithms, and the performance of considered regressors is compared. A real Li-Ion battery dataset is used to demonstrate the applicability. For the case of a bagging-based ensemble regressor, the method obtained a correlation coefficient of 0.9996.

articleTitle: The Usability of Teaching Practice Placement System Through Cloud Technology: PLMiSYS
abstract: Conventional teaching practice placement systems at universities often face inefficiencies, limited user-friendliness, and poor integration with modern technology, which restrict students from fully applying their theoretical knowledge in real teaching environments. To address these challenges, the PuLaMI Integrated System (PLMiSYS), a cloud-based placement management system, was developed by Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) to streamline the placement process. This study evaluates the usability of PLMiSYS, focusing on its effectiveness in meeting students’ needs. A mixed-method approach was employed, comprising quantitative data from usability surveys involving 285 students and qualitative data from semi-structured interviews with 15 students. Results show that PLMiSYS enhances placement efficiency, improves user satisfaction, and provides a scalable model for educational management. Participants highlighted the system’s intuitive design, though some suggested improvements for document upload capacity and integration with school systems. The study has practical implications, as PLMiSYS serves as a model for educational institutions aiming to digitise administrative processes, potentially reducing staff workload and increasing student satisfaction. Theoretically, this study adds to literature on technology adoption in education, demonstrating the importance of usability in cloud-based systems for effective educational management. Findings suggest that cloud technology adoption can improve operational efficiency and student placements, fostering a supportive learning environment.

articleTitle: Classifying Enzymatic Functions Using Graph Neural Networks: Insights from the ENZYMES Dataset
abstract: This study explores the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to classify enzyme functions using the ENZYMES dataset, which represents proteins and their interactions as graphs. The literature review highlights the evolution and efficacy of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in capturing complex relational data in graph structures, revolutionizing fields such as bioinformatics by facilitating advanced enzyme classification and potential drug discovery through enhanced analysis of biological interactions. The methodology uses the ENZYMES dataset from the TUDataset, which encodes protein structures into graphs for enzyme function classification. A structured Graph Neural Network was utilized with layers designed to capture complex graph hierarchies, employing preprocessing steps, advanced graph convolution techniques, and rigorous training procedures to ensure the model’s effectiveness and reproducibility in predicting enzyme functions. The study demonstrates that the Graph Neural Network model effectively learned and generalized enzyme function classification, as evidenced by consistent improvements in training performance and strong testing results. The model’s robustness was further validated through detailed analyses such as confusion matrices, ROC curves, and precision-recall metrics, which also identified specific areas for future improvement in feature engineering and training approaches to enhance accuracy and model interpretability.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Robotics: Revolutionizing Retail Store Automation and Beyond
abstract: AI in robotics involves the application of efficient algorithm and computational techniques that allows robots to operate independently, learn from the environment and make efficient decisions. However, in current studies, mostly contact methods that cannot be learned and do not respond to change are used despite the progress made in this regard. These approaches often fail to respond in real-time to а certain issue, which can result in inefficiency and low overall operational performance. To overcome these shortcomings, this paper presents a new technique in which DRL (Deep Reinforcement Learning) is used for motion control of a robotic arm and limb in retail automation. DRL allows the robotic system to learn the best motion profiles from playing a game with its surroundings with reduced chances of a less optimum setting due to changing environmental conditions. The most important peculiarities of the proposed approach include integration of enhanced neural structures and realization of automatic learning and decision-making. The effectiveness of the DRL approach is shown to be considerably higher than that of traditional ones, with accuracy reaching 99.3%. Such outcomes speak to the prospects to transform robotics through DRL knowledge and skills to enhance real-time adaptation and increase effectiveness. Lastly, this research enhances the existing literature in AI & Robotics and accordingly establishes the foundation for further developments of intelligent automation systems in various fields.

articleTitle: Centroid-Based Aspect Sentiment Analysis for MOOC Learner Reviews
abstract: Developing comprehensive analytics for Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) is essential for improving course design and enhancing learner engagement. In this work, we introduce MOOCSense, a multi-stage sentiment analysis module designed to analyze MOOC learner reviews and contribute to generating detailed MOOC analytics. In the first stage, we employ a mapping algorithm that extracts key MOOC-specific terms and central semantic phrases from the reviews. In the second stage, we propose a novel Centroid-Based Learning approach combined with the BERT (CLB) model to capture both implicit and explicit sentiment polarity in learner reviews, leveraging BERT’s deep contextual understanding of natural language. By focusing on the central semantics of each review, our approach uncovers the emotional drivers behind learner engagement or dissatisfaction. This dual-stage module enables more accurate sentiment association with specific course aspects, enriching MOOC analytics with valuable insights. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach across various MOOC datasets, achieving an accuracy of 92%, making it a promising solution for generating in-depth learning analytics and supporting course improvement strategies.

articleTitle: Engineering Education in a New Era: A Case Study in Saudi Arabia
abstract: COVID-19 Pandemic had impacted educational systems worldwide demanding major reforms to teaching strategies. Educators were forced to quickly adapt to remote learning and online teaching methods. This shift has highlighted the need for flexible and adaptable teaching strategies that can be implemented in traditional and virtual classrooms. Moreover, grasping attention of new generations requires more efforts in delivering knowledge and skills. With the rise of technology and social media, younger generations have become accustomed to receiving information in a fast-paced and visually engaging manner. This necessitates that educators implement ways to make learning more interactive, engaging, and relevant to students' lives. Experiential learning is a type of learning that involves hands-on experiences and active participation in the learning process taking many forms, such as internships, field trips, simulations, augmented reality and role-playing activities. AR/VR technology is recently playing a role in different educational activities. This study examines achievement levels and feedback reports of architectural and civil engineering students upon applying different experiential learning techniques. Students from these two main engineering disciplines worked together in a multidisciplinary project framework. Augmented reality activities were implemented using EON AR/VR Reality platform to create an engaging learning environment. The study is conducted by employing surveys to gauge students’ perception. Positive feedback was reported in addition to enhancement of understanding of topics.

articleTitle: IoT-enabled Student Attendance System using RISC-V based Embedded System
abstract: Inefficiencies, cumbersome processes, and a significant risk of errors, delays, and misuse often plague conventional methods for tracking student attendance. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a smart monitoring system driven by the Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT), specifically designed for resource-limited embedded processors. This research examines a real-time facial recognition-based student attendance tracking system implemented on an edge device. Additionally, it assesses the effectiveness of ARM and RISC-V microprocessors as the foundation for a reliable edge computing platform. The system employs Python’s Dlib library and the ResNet model for effective facial recognition. Comparisons between the Raspberry Pi Model 4 B and the RISC-V StarFive VisionFive2 are made to determine the optimal platform for extensive deployments. The proposed edge system emphasizes security, automation, and reliability, facilitating real-time, precise attendance tracking and significantly improving operational efficiency for educators and administrators. The solution using the RISC-V processor is at least 10 times more energy-efficient than the competing solution based on the RISC processor instruction set architecture.

articleTitle: Bridging Gender Disparities in Mental Health: A Bilingual Large Language Model for Multilingual Therapeutic Chatbots
abstract: Significant gender disparities and a general lack of support systems compound the state of mental health in developing countries. Women, in particular, face unique challenges due to societal norms and expectations that often restrict their access to mental health services. Additionally, the cultural stigma associated with mental health issues affects both men and women but can be particularly debilitating for women who may be less likely to seek help or disclose their struggles. This study explores the application of Jais-13B, a pre-existing bilingual Large Language Model (LLM) proficient in English and Arabic, tailored to address mental health inquiries. We employed a rich dataset encompassing both languages, essential for fine-tuning and enhancing Jais-13B’s responsiveness and empathetic engagement in mental health contexts. The optimization focused on improving the model’s ability to deliver accurate and contextually aware responses, which is crucial for effective mental health support. Performance evaluation using the cross-entropy loss function demonstrated that Jais-13B achieved an accuracy of 70.58%, indicating its capability to produce relevant and precise answers to mental health questions. These results showcase Jais-13B’s potential to enhance digital mental health interventions significantly, providing accessible care solutions across diverse linguistic landscapes. This study reaffirms the effectiveness of bilingual LLMs in mental health applications and provides insights into their practical implementation, setting a foundational benchmark for future research in multilingual therapeutic chatbots.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Diabetes Prediction Models: Leveraging Advanced Feature Reduction and Classification Methods
abstract: The global challenge of diabetes demands innovative approaches for early diagnosis and effective management. This paper investigates the integration of advanced dimensionality reduction and feature selection techniques to improve diabetes prediction models. Utilizing Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm, the study focuses on optimizing feature selection to enhance model accuracy, computational efficiency, and interpretability. Employing two diverse datasets—the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) and the Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset—the research evaluates the performance of Random Forest and Logistic Regression models. Results reveal significant improvements in predictive accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly with ABC-selected features, reducing feature dimensionality while maintaining high accuracy. This study underscores the potential of combining PCA and ABC to revolutionize predictive healthcare analytics, offering robust tools for diabetes management and prevention.

articleTitle: Classification of ECG Signals Using Machine Learning for Detection of Cardiac Abnormalities
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading cause of mortality worldwide, with arrhythmias contributing significantly to these statistics. This study proposes a machine learning framework for automated ECG classification, focusing on Premature Ventricular Contraction (PVC), Atrial Fibrillation (AFib), and Ventricular Tachycardia (VTach). Normal electrocardiogram (ECG) signals from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database were integrated with synthetically generated abnormal signals, which were derived using mathematical models and implemented in MATLAB. Signals were segmented into 1-second intervals, with features extracted including P-wave amplitude, QRS width, and T-wave frequency. A Random Forest classifier achieved 0.88 accuracy, with high precision and recall for each class, including normal, atrial fibrillation, and ventricular ectopic beats, demonstrating balanced performance across all categories. The incorporation of synthetic data addressed dataset imbalances, particularly improving detection of minority classes like VTach. The framework demonstrates potential for real-time implementation in wearable devices and telemedicine platforms. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and exploring deep learning techniques to enhance clinical applicability.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Advanced ECG Noise Reduction Filters
abstract: The study examined various filtering methods applied to ECG signals; the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia dataset included two channels to reduce noise and artifacts while maintaining critical waveform characteristics. Initial filtering included a notch filter and a bandpass filter. Advanced filters such as Savitzky-Golay, Wavelet, Kalman, Wiener, and combined Wiener-Golay were used for noise reduction. Results showed that the Kalman filter performed best with an average SNR of 21.40 dB, while the Wavelet method worked well on channel 2. The Wiener filter was less effective due to its limited adaptability to changing noise. The combined Wiener-Savitzky-Golay filter showed a balanced performance but did not outperform the Kalman filter. Visual inspections of ECG signals from five patients revealed that the Kalman and Wavelet filters successfully maintained crucial morphological characteristics. The Savitzky-Golay filter offered effective smoothing but sometimes dampened the QRS complex, while the Wiener filter introduced high-frequency artifacts.

articleTitle: Distributed Denial of Service Attack Detection by Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: The exponential expansion of computer networks and the internet makes it clear that there is a chance of being attacked and harmed. In the meantime, one of the most crucial defensive measures against the more complex and frequent network attacks is the intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDSs and IPSs). Due to insufficient datasets, anomaly-based research in intrusion detection systems is plagued by imprecise deployment, analysis, and evaluation. The researchers analyzed a variety of datasets, including DARPA98, KDD99, ISC2012, and ADFA13, to assess how well their suggested intrusion detection and intrusion prevention techniques performed. There are several issues: lack of adequate attack coverage, unrepresentative payloads, and anonymised packet information, insufficient traffic volume and diversity, or a deficiency in feature set and metadata. This study is focused on CICIDS-2017 which is the recently updated IDS dataset that meets real-world requirements and is accessible publicly. In addition to benign network flows and distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, it contains seven common attack network flows as well. To provide the optimal combination of features for the identification of the attack category, it also assesses the efficacy of several machine learning (ML) algorithms and network traffic feature sets. Even though various ML techniques like Linear Regression, Random Forests, and Decision Tree can be used, and performed very well, Hybrid Algorithm is designed to get better analysis on dataset.

articleTitle: Advancing Environmental Sustainability: Renewable Energy Transition, Carbon Footprint Reduction, and Emission Control Innovations
abstract: Combating climate change and promoting environmental sustainability necessitate a dedicated emphasis on renewable energy sources and lowering carbon footprints. Shifting from fossil fuels to renewable resources, such as solar, wind, biomass, and geothermal energy, is imperative. Equally important is enhancing energy efficiency across industries, transportation, buildings, and household appliances to reduce overall energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Technological advancements, such as improved energy storage and smart grid systems, are essential for boosting the efficiency and dependability of renewable energy sources. Strategies to lower carbon footprints include transitioning to clean transportation, optimizing land use, reducing waste, recycling, promoting sustainable agriculture, and implementing carbon offset initiatives. Public education, corporate responsibility, and personal environmental awareness play vital roles in supporting carbon reduction. By combining sustainable energy practices with carbon reduction measures, we can collectively work towards curbing climate change and fostering a sustainable future. Additionally, utilized techniques to address the problem of high air pollution during vehicle cold starts. We modeled catalytic converter dynamics in MATLAB Simulink, using simplifying assumptions. One significant assumption involved treating the catalytic converter as a Continuous Stirred-Tank Reactor (CSTR), which allowed us to model its temperature uniformly, without accounting for temperature changes along its length. This approach is aimed at saving lives and reducing costs by effectively minimizing air pollution.

articleTitle: Deep learning for sleep disorder diagnosis: Enhancing EEG Analysis with Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: The rising prevalence of sleep disorders highlights their disastrous effects on health, well-being, cognitive performance, memory, and learning outcomes. Sleep disorders such as insomnia and sleep apnea normally require extensive instrumentation and expertise for diagnosis, which is not always possible or even available in most cases. This work, therefore, proposes a state-of-the-art use of Machine Learning (ML) to develop a model for the classification and detection of sleep patterns from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. The model is trained on a synthetic dataset, developed using mathematical simulations of real-life EEG data. This is a novelty in this area, which allows this model to be precise yet robust without relying too much on real-world datasets.The application bridges advanced AI techniques with real-world applications and smooths out the experience for healthcare professionals and researchers alike. This research highlights how ML might transform sleep medicine through efficient, extended solutions for EEG data analysis and sleep disorder detection. We provide a realistic EEG simulation combined with an intuitive application, a powerful platform that makes advanced sleep diagnostics more accessible and impactful, which supports the development of educational strategies or technologies.
